newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries end higher, T-bond at 7-month high.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries end higher, T-bond at 7-month high.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries posted moderate gains and ended at new seven-month highs on Wednesday, as continued bullish sentiment and positive technicals lifted the market.
"The fact that we haven't really pulled back means people need to buy paper," said a head trader at a large U.S. primary dealership.
The 30-year bond closed at 100-27/32, up 9/32. Its yield declined to 6.56 percent from 6.59 percent -- its lowest level since December 10.
Highlighting an otherwise lackluster session was the Treasury's sale of five-year inflation-protected securities, known as TIPS.
The auction was deemed sloppy, even after the when-issued five-year TIPS note backed up 20 basis points the past two sessions to a sale price of 3.744 percent.
Yet, the market barely blinked when the results were announced.
"We have learned that the 'real' market has very little correlation to the TIPS market," said Patrick Dimick, Treasury market strategist at UBS Securities LLC.
Late Wednesday, the when-issued five-year TIPS note yield was down to 3.68 percent. Traders said that the post-auction decline meant the distribution of the issue went well.
And, added Darcy Bradbury, managing director at Bankers Trust and former Treasury official, the high 3.31 bid-to-cover-ratio suggested good demand for the issue.

"You have to look at it over the long term," said Bradbury, an architect of the TIPS market. "There was pretty broad-based participation ... the whole point was to get more people involved in the instrument, so this was a good start."

Treasuries gained from the start of trading, boosted by retail buying from Asia and, later, domestic accounts. Some players reported hedge fund buying in two- and five-year notes, and front-end buying by government agencies.
Trading activity was purely technical, since no key economic data are due out until Friday's June producer price report.
Gains were capped as "value traders" have become more vocal than "momentum traders," said Dimick. "We are reaching levels that are giving value some consideration," he said.

Volume was light at $73 billion, but nearly $20 billion above Tuesday, according to GovPX. Volume in TIPS was especially heavy -- with the five-year TIPS posting more than $1 billion -- albeit small compared with the more than $6.5 billion in regular five-year notes.

In late trading, the two-year note was at 100-7/32, up 2/32, to yield 5.88 percent. The five-year note was up 3/32 at 100-14/32 with a yield of 6.15 percent. The 10-year note closed up 5/32 at 102-24/32 to yield 6.25 percent.
The three-month bill was unchanged at 4.97 percent. The six-month bill was unchanged at 5.08 percent and the year-bill was down one basis point at 5.24 percent.
